# Independent audit: projection-normalized layer-cake lattice discrepancy



For the optional extension to infinitely many coarse fibers, the normalized numerical estimate necessarily retains a finite positive total `0<sum_z M_z<infinity`. This scope clarification was sent to the author; it does not affect the finite-family theorem.

## 1. Exact peak factor and charged boundaries

For s>=1, compactness of Q puts every section in a common bounded set. If u_j tends to u, every section Q_(u_j) eventually lies in any fixed small neighborhood of Q_u; otherwise a subsequence of violating section points would converge to a point of Q_u. Continuity of volumes of decreasing compact neighborhoods yields upper semicontinuity of the section-volume function. Thus its positive closed superlevel sets are compact, and Brunn--Minkowski makes them convex. This reasoning includes lower-dimensional sections, whose s-volume is zero.

The same facts apply to every closed cut Q intersect H. Its peak is at most the original peak F. Applying the exact lattice-count discrepancy in dimension r at every positive level and integrating gives

    |mu(H)-vol_(r+s)(Q intersect H)|
      <=2r delta(2R+2delta)^(r-1)F.

The exponent r-1 is correct: the integrated sets lie in the sampled projection space, not the full r+s dimensional body. Both Tonelli integrals equal the desired masses, including sampled boundary values: for every a>=0, the integral over t>0 of 1_(a>=t) is a. Using closed rather than open superlevels causes no level-integral error and is needed to apply the closed-set counting bound directly.

If F=0, both sampled and continuous masses are zero and the assertion is exact. If Q has zero full volume but F>0, the same absolute estimate still controls a possible positive sampled mass. For s=0 the function is precisely the indicator of the compact projection, so the theorem reduces to the r-dimensional counting discrepancy, including lower-dimensional and empty sets.

Restrictions of an ambient cap to a fixed coarse fiber may be empty or the entire fiber when the within-fiber normal vanishes. These cases satisfy the same bound, the entire-space case having been included explicitly and the empty case being immediate.

## 2. Peak-to-total constant

When M>0 and s>=1, the peak is attained and the projection has positive r-volume. For a maximizing u_0 and any u in the projection, convexity gives a translated copy of `(1-theta)Q_(u_0)` in the section at `(1-theta)u_0+theta u`; this remains valid if Q_u has zero s-volume because it is nonempty. Hence that section has volume at least `(1-theta)^s F`.

The t-superlevel therefore contains a homothetic projection copy of scale `1-(t/F)^(1/s)`. Layer cake yields exactly

    M >= F vol_r(P) / binom(r+s,r).

The substitution b=a^(1/s) makes the integral equal to

    s integral_0^1 b^(s-1)(1-b)^r db
      =s!r!/(r+s)!.

There is no missing scale or factorial. For s=0 and positive M, F=1 and the formula is the identity M=vol_r(P). Dividing the peak error by this lower bound produces precisely the projection-volume denominator in the stated relative estimate.

## 3. Projection-only affine normalization

The map `(u,x)->(Au+b,x)` leaves every s-dimensional section measure unchanged. It multiplies lattice covolume and full r+s dimensional volume by the same factor |det A|. Therefore both weighted sampled cap mass and full coarse cap mass acquire this factor, and normalized halfspace masses and depths are invariant. Every oblique halfspace transforms affinely; no restriction to vertical or horizontal cuts is introduced.

The maximal-simplex normalization has the stated projection radius R_r=r(r+2) and contains a unit r-ball. Substituting projection volume at least kappa_r into the relative bound gives

    e(r,s,eta)=[2r binom(r+s,r)/kappa_r]
                  eta(2R_r+2eta)^(r-1).

The same error controls total mass. If e<1, sampled mass is positive and the normalized cap error is bounded by 2e/(1-e), as stated. A transformed covering-radius bound supplies an appropriate Voronoi-cell cube, with only null boundaries needing assignment. No assertion that this covering radius automatically tends to zero is made.

## 4. Multiple maps as estimates, not a global source transformation

For a fixed original cap, the inequality for each positive-volume coarse fiber can be computed in its own normalized projection coordinates. Undoing that fiber's determinant gives its discrepancy in the common original measure. Summing the absolute estimates gives the stated mass-weighted average of the errors.

The argument does not require the maps A_z to agree, because they are used only to prove numerical inequalities in the original coordinates. It does not construct a transformed mixed body with those unrelated maps. A fixed finite family with every transformed cell radius tending to zero has a weighted error tending to zero, regardless of the size or limit of its total coarse volume. With a uniform error bound the same numerical summation extends to countable families having finite positive total mass.

A zero-full-volume coarse fiber falls outside the peak-to-total division. Its positive sampled mass must be covered by the absolute estimate or otherwise shown negligible. The note explicitly preserves this qualification. Uniform halfspace discrepancy also supplies no feasible sampled center by itself; the separate recovery hypothesis remains necessary.

No mathematical defect was found in the finite-family theorem or its constants.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
